correctness.rationale: For a bank with labels \(k_i\), each allowed online choice is a subset and therefore supplies one residue \(\sum_{i\in S}k_i\pmod{2^n-1}\). Universality with activation cap \(h\) forces the number of eligible subsets to be at least \(2^n-1\). The resulting integer inequalities give \(r\ge n\) and, when \(r=n\), \(h\ge n-1\). For the source labels \(a2^i\), multiplication by the unit \(a\) permutes residues, and every representative below \(2^n-1\) except the excluded all-ones integer has Hamming weight at most \(n-1\), proving sharpness. No finite experiment is used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The bound turns the source paper’s informal need for \(n\) selectable catalysts into a sharp architecture theorem and exactly identifies the register/activation frontier at the minimal bank size. This explains why a mere relabeling of the fixed kickback bank cannot obtain the later linear-size universal catalyst: the successful later method changes the online operation to a controlled power. The boundary is natural because it is tied directly to the \(2^n-1\) phase grid used by the construction, rather than to an arbitrary parameter slice.
